In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytosolic acetyl-CoA pool is mainly generated by the glyoxylateshunt and the peroxisomal pool is mainly derived from fatty acid oxidation.
the acetyl-CoA pool in S. cerevisiae is compartmentalized and that the distribution of acetyl-Coa between the cytosolic and the peroxisomal compartment is regulated by the carbon supply of the yeast.

the acetyl-CoA derived from cytosolic and/or peroxisomal citrate is used for the synthesis of fatty acid and sterol in the cytosol, while the acetyl-CoAs derived from the glyoxylateshuttle and the TCA cycle are used for the synthesisof fatty acid in the peroxisome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acetyl-CoA is a key metabolite in the central metabolism of yeast and is compartmentalized into cytosol and peroxisomes.
the cytosolic acetyl-CoA pool is mainly generated through glycolysis, whereas the peroxisomal pool is mainly generated via the glyoxylateshuttle.
the acetyl-CoA biosynthesis and the glyoxylated shunt in S. cerevisiae are compartmentalized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acetyl-CoA pool in yeast is highly regulated, and the distribution of acetyl-CoAs is highly dynamic and depends on the carbon source.
acetyl-CoA is a key intermediate for carbon metabolism and its metabolism is compartmentalised.
acetyl-CoA distribution between cytosol and peroxisomes is a dynamic process, and is affected by the carbon sources.
